newsitem.title: FINLAND: Nokia leads Helsinki ahead, Hartwall soars.
newsitem.headline: Nokia leads Helsinki ahead, Hartwall soars.

text.p: Shares ended lively trade higher for a third straight day on Thursday, buoyed by early gains in Nokia on Wall Street and sharp gains in insurers amid talk of a shake-up in the Finnish sector, brokers said.
The HEX index rose 0.75 percent to m2,163.51, with volume a lively 417 million, nearly half of it in Nokia which picked up 3.50 markka to 202.50.
Bulls held the ground for most of the session, but at the close the picture was clouded by early losses in New York.

Hartwall advanced sharply after a positive surprise in its January-August profits -- up 230 percent. It ended lively trade up 11.00 markka or almost nine percent at 134.00, and brokers still saw scope for more gains on Friday.

Insurers Pohjola and Sampo advanced in active trade as speculation spread that Merita bank, which has major holdings in both companies, might be looking to sell -- possibly to another Nordic financial services company.
Pohjola's B share ended at 91.10 markka, up 2.10, after touching a two-year high of 94.00. Sampo held gains to closed at a two-year high of 322.00 markka, up 3.00.
The speculation took Merita up 0.13 markka to 9.89 amid hopes it would boost its returns by selling the assets.
But forestries remained under heavy pressure following Metsa-Serla's earnings warning on Tuesday.
"There was massive selling, particularly in Metsa-Serla, by foreign investors," one broker said.
Metsa-Serla's B share lost 0.80 markka at 30.00.
However, UPM managed to end up 0.50 markka at 96.50 in brisk trade, with investors bargain-hunting after recent losses.
